Cell footprint smaller: DMSO cells broad flat polygons; treated cells compact, star/spindle shaped, long processes. Green tubulin and red actin area per cell visibly reduced.

F-actin red: DMSO diffuse peripheral belt with low variation. Treated: brighter, patchy red rims, spiky filopodia/lamellipodia and star-like outlines. Increased heterogeneity and intensity visible in colour.

Beta-tubulin green: DMSO diffuse uniform green network filling cytoplasm. Treated: brighter green, more textured/punctate, heterogeneous, perinuclear brightening and rounded mitotic cells with condensed tubulin.

Nuclei blue DAPI: DMSO round/oval uniform, single per cell. Treated: many irregular, lobed, cleft nuclei with reduced circularity/solidity. Increased bright small round cells with condensed chromosomes/yellow overlap of DAPI+tubulin+actin, consistent with mitotic arrest/failed division - ~5-10 per treated field vs 1-2 in DMSO.
Cell outline irregular/spiky: DMSO smooth polygonal solidity; treated irregular stellate borders.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: ALLN (Protein degradation / proteasome + calpain inhibitor) - our conclusion Microtubule stabilizers p=0.60-0.62 was incorrect. This was a phenotype mimic case leading to overcall.

What the evidence got right:
We did detect a real high-dose cytoskeletal/cell-cycle stress phenotype. Wells w_a72fe93741 (100 uM, e2) tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.0, nuc_solidity z=-15.5, act_std z=+14.6 and w_daa103d348 (10 uM, e3) tub_glcm_contrast +21.9, nuc_solidity -23.7, act_std +10.8 with multinucleation and density lower in describe_phenotype e5 were genuine. Review confirms 100 uM taxol/etoposide controls show the expected tubulin-texture and nuclear-size signature, so the imaging quantitation pipeline was working. Intermediate dose w_b9bba7558b (3 uM, e14) nuc_major_axis +15.2, nuc_area +9.8, cell_major_axis +6.5 with describe_phenotype e20 density similar, unknown candidate, and compare_to_reference_atlas e19 DNA damage 7/10, DNA replication 3/10 was also correctly measured - we recorded a G2-like nuclear enlargement. Dose_response e10 nuc_dna_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 and e26 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 were real accrual signals.

What misled and what we missed:
1. Atlas bias + non-specific texture readout: e6 Microtubule stabilizers 5/10 and e24 6/10 at high doses dominated our hypothesis updates e13 and e27. Extremely high tub_glcm_contrast (e2, e3, e7 rho=+1.00, e15 rho=+0.80, e26 tub_mean) looked definitive for bundling. We missed that proteasome inhibition stabilizes cytoskeletal and cell-cycle regulators and can produce identical texture/actin heterogeneity as secondary consequence, not direct tubulin engagement. This is mechanistically plausible: ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation regulates cyclins and cell cycle arrest PMID 11864973 and differential stability of D-type cyclins degraded by proteasome PMID 15125768, and proteasome inhibition stabilizes proteins PMID 26639105. The crosstalk is known: microtubule-targeting agents themselves induce proteasomal degradation of tubulin PMID 19665001, illustrating why the readouts overlap.

2. Dismissing contradicting intermediate dose: e19 DNA damage signature at 3 uM and e14 nuclear enlargement were listed as contradicting evidence in hypothesis history but we rationalized them as "secondary G2/M arrest precursor not primary DNA damage" e21/e22. In fact that intermediate phenotype was the clue to protein accumulation / proteotoxic G2 arrest rather than stabilizer bundling. Multinucleation e8 rho=+0.50 p=0.67, nuc_solidity e9 rho=-0.50 p=0.67, cell_count e11 rho=-0.50 p=0.67, frac_mitotic_like e12 rho=+0.87 p=0.33, nuc_area e16 rho=-0.40 p=0.6, nuc_dna_integrated e17 rho=+0.20 p=0.8, cell_area e18 rho=-0.80 p=0.2 were all non-significant (p 0.2-0.8) on n=3-4 wells, indicating underpowered monotonic trends. We treated weak rho values as supporting microtubule stabilizer direction while ignoring lack of significance and moderate per-well cell counts (95-213 cells at high dose, e2/e3) indicating cytotoxic loss.

3. Acquisition choice error: list_available_experiments e1 8 doses, 4 wells total - we acquired only 4 wells in a dose-response ladder (e2-e4, e14) and spent the entire budget (e23 0 of 4 left) before testing specificity. Review verdict request_experiment was correct: confidence remained limited by moderate sample size and morphology-only readouts without target engagement. The requested discriminating check - a non-inducer perturbation control arm matched for dose/time/DMSO parallel to taxol/etoposide and a microtubule destabilizer arm - would have falsified specificity. We could not run it due to spent budget e28. We also never acquired low-dose 0.03-0.3 uM wells to test threshold reversibility.

4. Knowledge base gap: lookup_compound e29/e30 showed no curated ChEMBL mechanisms and CID mismatch (name CID 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339). Literature searches e31-e34 after unblinding returned ALLN/calpain/proteasome hits, but atlas had no strong proteasome inhibitor reference to map to, so our prior heavily weighted microtubule classes by default. Correct next step per our own key_evidence but unexecuted: acetyl-tubulin, p-H3, gammaH2AX, flow DNA content, in vitro tubulin polymerization, plus proteasome activity/ubiquitinated protein readout.
what_was_right: High-dose tubulin texture + actin heterogeneity + irregular multinucleate nuclei were real (e2 z+28, e3 z+21.9, e5 lower density)
Intermediate 3uM nuclear enlargement (e14 +15.2 major axis) and DNA damage atlas call (e19 7/10) correctly measured G2-like arrest
Control check cited in review valid - pipeline detects microtubule stabilizer signature at high dose when present
what_was_wrong: Interpreted non-specific proteostasis stress texture as direct microtubule engagement (e6, e24, e7, e26)
Discounted e19 DNA damage signal and non-significant dose trends e8-e12, e16-e18 as secondary
Exhausted 4-well budget on dose-response without reserving control arm (e23), leaving request_experiment impossible (e28)

## Reflection

Unblinded truth: ALLN (Protein degradation / proteasome + calpain inhibitor) - our conclusion Microtubule stabilizers p=0.60-0.62 was incorrect. This was a phenotype mimic case leading to overcall.

What the evidence got right:
We did detect a real high-dose cytoskeletal/cell-cycle stress phenotype. Wells w_a72fe93741 (100 uM, e2) tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.0, nuc_solidity z=-15.5, act_std z=+14.6 and w_daa103d348 (10 uM, e3) tub_glcm_contrast +21.9, nuc_solidity -23.7, act_std +10.8 with multinucleation and density lower in describe_phenotype e5 were genuine. Review confirms 100 uM taxol/etoposide controls show the expected tubulin-texture and nuclear-size signature, so the imaging quantitation pipeline was working. Intermediate dose w_b9bba7558b (3 uM, e14) nuc_major_axis +15.2, nuc_area +9.8, cell_major_axis +6.5 with describe_phenotype e20 density similar, unknown candidate, and compare_to_reference_atlas e19 DNA damage 7/10, DNA replication 3/10 was also correctly measured - we recorded a G2-like nuclear enlargement. Dose_response e10 nuc_dna_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 and e26 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 were real accrual signals.

What misled and what we missed:
1. Atlas bias + non-specific texture readout: e6 Microtubule stabilizers 5/10 and e24 6/10 at high doses dominated our hypothesis updates e13 and e27. Extremely high tub_glcm_contrast (e2, e3, e7 rho=+1.00, e15 rho=+0.80, e26 tub_mean) looked definitive for bundling. We missed that proteasome inhibition stabilizes cytoskeletal and cell-cycle regulators and can produce identical texture/actin heterogeneity as secondary consequence, not direct tubulin engagement. This is mechanistically plausible: ubiquitin/proteasome-dependent degradation regulates cyclins and cell cycle arrest PMID 11864973 and differential stability of D-type cyclins degraded by proteasome PMID 15125768, and proteasome inhibition stabilizes proteins PMID 26639105. The crosstalk is known: microtubule-targeting agents themselves induce proteasomal degradation of tubulin PMID 19665001, illustrating why the readouts overlap.

2. Dismissing contradicting intermediate dose: e19 DNA damage signature at 3 uM and e14 nuclear enlargement were listed as contradicting evidence in hypothesis history but we rationalized them as "secondary G2/M arrest precursor not primary DNA damage" e21/e22. In fact that intermediate phenotype was the clue to protein accumulation / proteotoxic G2 arrest rather than stabilizer bundling. Multinucleation e8 rho=+0.50 p=0.67, nuc_solidity e9 rho=-0.50 p=0.67, cell_count e11 rho=-0.50 p=0.67, frac_mitotic_like e12 rho=+0.87 p=0.33, nuc_area e16 rho=-0.40 p=0.6, nuc_dna_integrated e17 rho=+0.20 p=0.8, cell_area e18 rho=-0.80 p=0.2 were all non-significant (p 0.2-0.8) on n=3-4 wells, indicating underpowered monotonic trends. We treated weak rho values as supporting microtubule stabilizer direction while ignoring lack of significance and moderate per-well cell counts (95-213 cells at high dose, e2/e3) indicating cytotoxic loss.

3. Acquisition choice error: list_available_experiments e1 8 doses, 4 wells total - we acquired only 4 wells in a dose-response ladder (e2-e4, e14) and spent the entire budget (e23 0 of 4 left) before testing specificity. Review verdict request_experiment was correct: confidence remained limited by moderate sample size and morphology-only readouts without target engagement. The requested discriminating check - a non-inducer perturbation control arm matched for dose/time/DMSO parallel to taxol/etoposide and a microtubule destabilizer arm - would have falsified specificity. We could not run it due to spent budget e28. We also never acquired low-dose 0.03-0.3 uM wells to test threshold reversibility.

4. Knowledge base gap: lookup_compound e29/e30 showed no curated ChEMBL mechanisms and CID mismatch (name CID 6915732 vs BBBC021 structure CID 21118339). Literature searches e31-e34 after unblinding returned ALLN/calpain/proteasome hits, but atlas had no strong proteasome inhibitor reference to map to, so our prior heavily weighted microtubule classes by default. Correct next step per our own key_evidence but unexecuted: acetyl-tubulin, p-H3, gammaH2AX, flow DNA content, in vitro tubulin polymerization, plus proteasome activity/ubiquitinated protein readout.

What was right:
- High-dose tubulin texture + actin heterogeneity + irregular multinucleate nuclei were real (e2 z+28, e3 z+21.9, e5 lower density)
- Intermediate 3uM nuclear enlargement (e14 +15.2 major axis) and DNA damage atlas call (e19 7/10) correctly measured G2-like arrest
- Control check cited in review valid - pipeline detects microtubule stabilizer signature at high dose when present

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted non-specific proteostasis stress texture as direct microtubule engagement (e6, e24, e7, e26)
- Discounted e19 DNA damage signal and non-significant dose trends e8-e12, e16-e18 as secondary
- Exhausted 4-well budget on dose-response without reserving control arm (e23), leaving request_experiment impossible (e28)

Proposed next experiment: Repeat with matched non-inducer perturbation + microtubule destabilizer (nocodazole/vinblastine) control arms, plus target-engagement readouts: proteasome activity, ubiquitin Western, acetyl-tubulin, p-H3, gammaH2AX, tubulin polymerization assay across 0.03-100uM
